# DataSQRL

> DataSQRL is an open-source data engineering harness for building data engineering agents designed around human control, correctness, and safety. It extends coding agents with a SQL compiler, a validator, an event-time simulator, and skills. The compiler turns SQRL scripts into complete data pipelines that integrate Kafka, Flink, PostgreSQL, Iceberg, and GraphQL, REST, and MCP APIs.

Key facts for working with DataSQRL:

- A project is one or more `.sqrl` scripts plus `*package.json` configuration files. SQRL is Flink SQL extended with `IMPORT`/`EXPORT` statements, table functions, relationships, and hints; the SQRL Language page documents only what differs from Flink SQL.
- The DataSQRL CLI is distributed as the `datasqrl/cmd` Docker image with the `compile`, `test`, and `run` commands. `compile` validates the script and generates every deployment asset, `test` runs the pipeline and the test queries and compares their results to snapshots, and `run` compiles and runs the pipeline locally in Docker.
- Configuration files are deep-merged in the order given on the command line, on top of the default configuration.
- System functions are always available; library functions must be imported with `IMPORT stdlib.<library>.<function>;`.

This is the documentation of DataSQRL v0.11, an older release. The documentation of the latest release is at https://docs.datasqrl.com/llms.txt.

## Overview

- [DataSQRL Documentation](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/v0-11/intro.md): DataSQRL is an open-source data engineering harness that provides guardrails and feedback for AI coding agents to build reliable data pipelines, data APIs (REST, MCP, GraphQL), and data products.

## Getting Started

- [Getting Started with DataSQRL](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/v0-11/intro/getting-started.md): The easiest way to understand how DataSQRL provides guardrails and feedback for AI coding agents is to build a data pipeline.

## Core Concepts

- [SQRL Language Specification](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/v0-11/sqrl-language.md): SQRL is an extension of Flink SQL that adds support for table functions and convenience syntax to build reactive data processing and serving applications.
- [Connecting External Data Sources and Sinks](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/v0-11/connectors.md): Use `CREATE TABLE` statements to connect external data sources and sinks with your SQRL script using the `WITH` clause to provide connector configuration.
- [Designing the Interface](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/v0-11/interface.md): Based on the SQRL script, DataSQRL generates the interface for the compiled data pipeline.
- [DataSQRL Configuration (`package.json` file)](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/v0-11/configuration.md): DataSQRL projects are configured with one or more `*package.json` files which are merged in the order they are provided to the DataSQRL command – latter files override fields in earlier ones, objec...
- [Flink Engine Configuration](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/v0-11/configuration-engine/flink.md): Apache Flink is a streaming and batch data processor that serves as the core data processing engine in DataSQRL pipelines.
- [Kafka Engine Configuration](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/v0-11/configuration-engine/kafka.md): Apache Kafka is a streaming data platform that serves as the log engine in DataSQRL pipelines for handling data streams and event logs.
- [Vert.x Engine Configuration](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/v0-11/configuration-engine/vertx.md): Eclipse Vert.x is a reactive server framework that serves as the GraphQL API server, routing queries to the backing database/log engines.
- [PostgreSQL Engine Configuration](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/v0-11/configuration-engine/postgres.md): PostgreSQL is a realtime database that stores the materialized views and tables generated by your DataSQRL pipeline for low-latency querying.
- [Iceberg Engine Configuration](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/v0-11/configuration-engine/iceberg.md): Apache Iceberg is an analytic database format that provides ACID transactions, schema evolution, and time travel capabilities for large analytic datasets.
- [Iceberg Query Engine Configurations](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/v0-11/configuration-engine/iceberg-query.md): Apache Iceberg stores analytic data but does not execute queries.
- [Default DataSQRL `package.json` Configuration](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/v0-11/configuration-default.md): The following is the default configuration file that user provided configuration files are merged on top of.
- [Cloud Deployment Configuration](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/v0-11/configuration-engine/cloud-deployment.md): Configures the cloud resources for each engine when deploying pipelines to DataSQRL Cloud.
- [Functions](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/v0-11/functions.md): SQRL supports all of Flink's built-in system functions.
- [System Functions](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/v0-11/functions-system-generated.md): DataSQRL provides built-in system functions that are available in all SQRL scripts.
- [Library Functions](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/v0-11/functions-library-generated.md): DataSQRL provides extended library functions that can be imported into your SQRL scripts.
- [DataSQRL Command](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/v0-11/compiler.md): The DataSQRL command initializes, compiles, runs, and tests SQRL projects.
- [Key DataSQRL Concepts](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/v0-11/intro/concepts.md): This document explains some of the key concepts in streaming data processing.

## Examples

- [DataSQRL Examples](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/v0-11/intro/examples.md): These examples demonstrate how AI coding agents use DataSQRL to build production-grade data products from data catalog definitions.

## How To

- [Project Structure](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/v0-11/howto/project-structure.md): A DataSQRL project is structured as follows where `{name}` is the project name.
- [Enriching Data Streams](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/v0-11/howto/stream-enrichment.md): A common requirement in stream processing is to enrich a STREAM of events with dimensional data in a time-consistent manner.
- [Templating](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/v0-11/howto/templating.md): DataSQRL uses the Mustache templating engine to substitute configuration variables in SQRL scripts, making them reusable and configurable without modifying the code.
- [Testing Authorization](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/v0-11/howto/testing-authorization.md): You can test record filtering, data masking, and other types of authorization based data access control with DataSQRL's automated test runner via the `test` command.
- [Testing](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/v0-11/howto/testing.md): DataSQRL's automated test runner can execute two types of tests via the `test` command
